# CLAUDE.md includes that resolve and never load

Measured 2026-09-13 in Claude Code on Windows. Every project wired to the shared
baseline had carried an include like this for months:

```
@D:\Claude Co worker\Token Save Manager Source\templates\project-baseline.md
```

The file existed, a parser resolved it, the Manager's panel said "chain
resolves" - and no session ever loaded a byte of it. Nothing raised. The only
place the truth showed was the session transcript's list of loaded instruction
files, which stopped one file short.

## Symptom

Rules you wrote in an included file are ignored. The agent behaves as if the
file does not exist, because for it, it does not.

## Cause: two separate gates, both silent

Canaries (`ZEBRA-<case>-7731` in each included file, then `claude -p "print
every ZEBRA- string"`):

| Include | Loaded |
|---|---|
| `@rel.md` (inside the project) | yes |
| `@sub\ dir/spaced.md` (escaped space, inside) | yes |
| `@C:/.../proj/abs.md` with `\ ` escapes (inside) | yes |
| `@C:\...\proj\abs.md` - backslashes, no spaces, inside | **no** |
| `@C:/.../proj space/abs.md` - raw spaces, inside | **no** |
| `@C:/outside/file.md` (no spaces), not approved | **no** |
| same, with `hasClaudeMdExternalIncludesApproved: true` | yes |
| `@link/file.md` where `link` is a junction to outside | **no** |
| `@hard.md`, a hardlink to an outside file | yes (fragile) |

1. **Spelling.** A backslash is only valid as the escape in `\ `, and a space
   must be escaped. A Windows path pasted as-is loads nothing.
2. **Location.** A file outside the project loads only after the project's
   record in `~/.claude.json` approves external includes. The desktop Code tab
   never showed that prompt. A junction does not get around it: the link is
   resolved to its real location first.

## Fix

Keep included files inside the project and spell includes relatively with
forward slashes. For a file shared across projects, commit a copy in each
project and regenerate it from the source (TokenSave Manager's Localize does
this for its baseline, with a sha header so a hand edit is never overwritten).
Do not rely on a hardlink: any tool that saves by writing a new file and
renaming it over the old one silently breaks the link.

## How to check a project

Look at a session transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<key>/<id>.jsonl`): the first
`attachment` of type `instructions` lists every file that loaded. If an include
is not there, it did not load, whatever any checker says.
